sources.note: Shows that a perturbation-based selection rule's apparent 31.8-point gain over majority voting in vision-language test-time scaling is a decoding-format effect, by adding a control that spends the same short-answer budget on the unperturbed image and finds it matches or beats the perturbation rule everywhere.
sources.title: It's the Decoding Format, Not the Perturbation: Auditing Consistency-Based Selection for Vision-Language Test-Time Scaling

sources.note: Reformulates chart question answering as a chain in which every reasoning step carries a predicted image region, trains that pairing through a curriculum graded by nesting depth, and finds explicit intermediate grounding worth 8.78 points over letting the model attend implicitly.
sources.title: CURV: Enhancing Chart Understanding Through Curriculum Visual Grounded Reasoning

sources.note: Splits a video model's latent computation into perception latents that always ground the question in visual evidence and reasoning latents allocated only when the question needs inference, and shows that reasoning latents without rationale supervision are worse than no reasoning latents at all.
sources.title: Perception Before Reasoning: Dynamic Latent Reasoning for Video Understanding and Question Answering

sources.note: Splits a spatial-reasoning chain of thought into explicitly typed segments -- perception, including depth, and reasoning -- and gives each its own process reward and its own advantage term, so that the two do not compete for credit under a single outcome signal.
sources.title: SCOUT: Unlocking Enhanced Spatial Reasoning via Structured Chain-of-Thought and Multi-Objective Process Reward

result.definition: Tying a reasoning step or a generated mention to a specific region of an image, and across 4 sources the property that separates multimodal reasoning from text reasoning with a picture attached. Its measured value: pairing every reasoning step with a predicted image region beats letting the model attend implicitly by 8.78 points, which those authors read as grounding earning its place as an intermediate vision-reasoning bridge rather than as the final objective -- and their ablation among grounding realisations finds masking beating boxing with cropping competitive at up to 7.93 points despite a sixteenfold resolution reduction. Two negative results bound it. Replacing a visual task token with language-encoded instructions costs 8.6 points, so the grounding must be visual rather than described. And an attended region is not a grounded one: what separates real from hallucinated objects is whether the attended region decodes to the target token, not whether it was attended.
